julia_customer: Hey team — EU customers seeing 2000+ms p95 and some 401 spikes for API keys that are definitely EU-only. Our billing page also shows requests attributed to us-east. Any idea?
anna_support: sorry you're hitting this, can you share a few request IDs and a repro curl?
julia_customer: sure, example request id req_20260317_01, timestamp 2026-03-17T10:12Z. Quick repro: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` — headers show `x-region: eu-west-1` expected but response headers include `x-region: us-east-1`.
mike_sre: curious — do you see any DNS differences from the client side? can you run `dig +short service.redwood.example @<client-resolver>` and `dig +short @8.8.8.8`?
julia_customer: ran from users in DE, here's one: 
```
> dig +short service.redwood.example @10.0.0.1
93.184.216.34
> dig +short service.redwood.example @8.8.8.8
93.184.216.34
```
(ips are examples)
raj_netops: that looks like the same A record, but that doesn't tell us POP. we rely on GeoIP + Anycast + EDNS-client-subnet to pick EU POP. if the ISP strips EDNS or we get stale GeoIP DB mapping it can route you to a us POP.
anna_support: customer reports auth 401 spikes — could misroute to a POP without their API key provisioning or a different auth shard.
mike_sre: can you curl with `-v` and capture `x-redwood-pop` and `x-auth-shard` headers? also check `traceroute -w 1 -m 10 service.redwood.example`
julia_customer: added headers from a failing request: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-redwood-pop: us-east-1a
x-auth-shard: shard-3
x-cache: MISS
x-request-id: req_20260317_01
```
we expect `eu-west-1b` and `shard-1`.
raj_netops: ok that nails it — request hitting us-east. two hypotheses: 1) ISP resolver returning an anycast IP that's tied to us-east via our loadbalancer's routing, or 2) EDNS client-subnet was stripped so our GeoIP fallback mapped to us-east. any chance the ISP is doing DNS over HTTPS with their own edns handling?
julia_customer: many of our users are on ISP-X which recently rolled out a new resolver.
mike_sre: can you share a `dig +trace service.redwood.example` from a problematic client? also `dig +short TXT _region.service.redwood.example @<resolver>` — we sometimes publish region hints for debugging.
julia_customer: trace attached: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +trace service.redwood.example
. 50322 IN NS a.root-servers.net.
...
93.184.216.34 ; from NS
```
no EDNS info shown.
raj_netops: sounds like resolver not passing EDNS-client-subnet. we can detect that in logs: mike, can you grep edge logs for req_20260317_01 and check `resolver_info` fields?
mike_sre: grabbing logs now — snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T10:12:34Z req_20260317_01 resolver=10.0.0.1 edns_csub=none chosen_pop=us-east-1a auth_shard=shard-3
```
so EDNS-client-subnet missing. fallback used GeoIP on the resolver IP -> mapped to us-east.
anna_support: is there any quick mitigation while we investigate? customers need EU routing and correct billing attribution.
raj_netops: short-term we can force regional pinning by honoring `X-Region-Hint` header for authenticated requests from this org. would need a config patch — low risk. medium-term: push a change to use our per-request fallback that prefers EU for EU-configured orgs even if resolver maps elsewhere.
mike_sre: agree. also we should refund misattributed billing for the window. I'll open an internal rollback-safe rollout to add org-pin header handling and an alert if EDNS is missing for >10% of requests from an org.
anna_support: noted — I'll open the billing escalation and let the customer know a timeline.
julia_customer: thanks. also, is there any public-facing test we can run to detect ISPs stripping EDNS? customers could self-check.
raj_netops: yes — ask them to run: 
```
dig +short @1.1.1.1 ct.service.redwood.example; dig +short @<their-resolver> ct.service.redwood.example
```
where `ct.service.redwood.example` is a special TXT we serve showing the EDNS client-subnet if present. if results differ, resolver strips EDNS.
mike_sre: I'm going to add an internal ticket: INF-4287 EDNS stripped by ISP-X causing EU->US POP misroute; mitigation: org region pin + billing audit. cc @sre-bot to create incident channel.
sre-bot: Incident channel created #inc-4287-edns-misroute
cloudflare-bot: Notified Cloudflare account team — potential resolver/DoH change at ISP-X.
anna_support: I'll update the customer with repro steps and expected timeframe ~4 hours for patch + billing audit. :thumbsup:
julia_customer: appreciated — we'll run the dig checks and report back.
mike_sre: follow-ups: add metric for `edns_missing_ratio` per org, backfill for last 24h to scope impact, and temporary org-pin rollout.
raj_netops: also schedule a sync with infra to examine GeoIP mapping for common resolvers; if mappings are stale we need updates.
anna_support: closing loop: customer notified, mitigation planned, billing flagged. will post updates here. :white_check_mark:
